analysis:
The only changed hunk in this file (head lines ~1260-1264, outside the supplied base excerpts, which end at line 630) is a test-only update. The `require` for ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine now passes `publicModels: []`, and the test name says "records only, no public declaration". The supplied base units 1-630 contain no changed lines. I reviewed them as surrounding context: the guided-flow placement checks, hand-off opt-in env parsing, developer-only forced-mode, bench-cap and bench-chip release-build refusals, served-build scoping of speed records, and qualified-shape records. They are test fixtures with synthetic keys, hashes and IPs, and contain no secrets and no production code paths.

The change adds no attack surface in this file. The signature change to publicTrafficLine, which now takes a publicModels parameter, implies a production-side change in the cluster library. That change is not supplied: public-traffic qualification now depends on a public-model declaration. It sits outside the retained threat IDs, which cover the provider and TB-011 and TB-007 areas, and it was not examined. The next pass should confirm that this parameter is a fail-closed gate on public traffic: an empty list must not qualify, and a record-only pass must not be treated as public authorization. The test asserts the not-yet-qualified behavior only for the pipeline family, with the phase-split family still qualified under empty publicModels. This is a test expectation, not evidence of a regression. No findings are raised, but the production counterpart should get a look from a reviewer who has it.
